doc.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022

title: Woody Herman's character and playing
summary: Herman was unfazed by his money troubles, loved cheese sandwiches and played clarinet and alto in Hodges' style; Rowe recalls seeing the band in Rochester.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: It’s too bad he had such a bad experience with finances and so forth. Do you think it wore him down?

No. No. It didn’t even faze him. Really it didn’t. He never really complained about it or anything. No. Never. Never. He just went on with — he loved his cheese sandwich at night after the gig and he had this vodka in the bin on the bus and really he always looked forward to that. No of course I mean he never complained about anything, about all his money or anything like that and all the problems that he went through. You know they got his house and all that sort of thing you know, up in Beverly Hills. I don’t know. No, he never felt really that it was bothering him too much.
That’s a good way to be.

He just loved to play. And he was a great clarinet player at the beginning. He played a lot of good things. I mean his alto playing I mean he admired Johnny Hodges. He was just as slurpy as Johnny. I mean he could tie a note and sail up to it.
I think there’s a good chance I saw you with the band around 19 — it could have been ’69 or ’70 in Rochester, New York.
It was outside and I always remember that Woody played the alto without a neck strap. It’s funny the things you remember.
